purpose: City v2 concept for review; not gameplay art or a collision map

prompts.prompt:
Create a polished production concept painting of the whole toy-town map for a premium children's 3D puzzle game, as an EDIT of reference image 1's board layout. Reference 1 is the existing playable city screenshot: preserve the board topology and general placement; remove all HUD, text, rings, grids, debug content, and interface. Reference 2 is the approved building STYLE and palette: beautifully sculpted rounded cream trim, terracotta/teal/slate tile roofs, soft painted toy materials, friendly shaped doors and windows, readable toy silhouettes. Reference 3 is a density and craft-quality reference from the same game's farm; match its delightful richness while using URBAN landscaping, not a forest farm. No writing, letters, labels, numbers or logos. Wide landscape, overhead three-quarter view, entire rectangular board visible with a narrow pale warm background, fill the frame, high clarity, soft warm daylight.

Layout is 110 units wide x 75 deep; north at back/top, south at front/bottom. Keep a rectangular asphalt road ring around a CENTRAL small green park: road centerlines x=-20/+20, z=-12/+12, road width6. Park boundary x=-16.5..16.5,z=-8.5..8.5 unchanged. Four road exits run from side centers to board edges. A straight tram track spans left-to-right near the front at z27 with a coral-and-cream tram and small stop. A narrow blue canal runs from the back to a little harbor in the southeast at x37, with one working drawbridge across the east-west street near z0. Keep the canal straight. These routes must stay unobstructed.

Build dense but carefully organized streets rather than isolated houses in a giant blank beige field. Put attractive 2-3 storey houses in rows along the BACK and FRONT edges and street frontages, with gardens behind, tree-lined pavement pockets, planter islands, benches and tactile raised curbs. Keep open paved courtyards directly in front of each task building for a child to place devices, no piles of mini props in those courts. Group flowers into readable color patches, avoid excessive tiny detail and crowded overlap.

Zones locked to the existing layout:
Back-left: a warm yellow three-storey grandmother's townhouse around (-44,-27), woman on its RIGHT-side balcony and compact basket lift beside it. Immediately to the right, two small residential houses. Bakery near(-12,-27): cream storefront with coral roof and teal striped awning, baker and a small bread belt/counter in its front courtyard. School near(11,-30) with blue pitched roof and clock; leave the paved school court toward(20,-20) empty and clear for laser/mirror play.
Middle-left: small parking court near(-40,-10) and bright toy lifting barrier near(-34,-4.5), little cars spaced apart. Car wash with two colorful brushes near(-38,8), construction plot and friendly tower crane near(-38,20), clearly separated from tracks.
Center park: fountain at(-3,1), modest Ferris wheel near(7,-3), a little wind generator near(12,3); a curving kitten path along WEST side with three lamps. Tree canopies frame the park without covering the wheel, fountain or free play areas.
Right of the park, left of canal: red fire station near(29,8) and fire engine facing its exit, safe open forecourt.
Far right strip beyond canal: toy shop near(49,-27), mint/teal music club near(48.5,-13) with a STAR-shaped sign instead of lettering, open club forecourt; a warm yellow rescue house near(48,8) with a cat on roof and fire ladder beside it (no dramatic fire). Small bins behind toy shop and a clearly unobstructed raccoon's back alley from upper-right corner.
Bottom: compact rows of townhouse fronts and planting along the track; reserve switch/substation play pocket in bottom-left and do not place houses on tracks. Harbor has one small friendly boat.

Use the same exquisitely modeled toy forms as reference2, hand-finished but clean and premium. Houses and props are volumetric with convincing shading, no flat billboard trees, no primitive gray box buildings, no floating objects, no transparent roofs. Connected roads and recognizable coherent blocks. Art-direct the density through grouped buildings and small garden courts, not random clutter. This is an aspirational concept, not a literal UI screenshot or an architectural diagram.

Edit this toy-town concept conservatively. Preserve its beautiful rendered toy style, all building designs, colors, camera, complete board framing, tram line, canal, ring road, street grid, grandmother townhouse, bakery, school, club, toyshop, firestation and rescue house. Change ONLY these two placement mistakes to match the playable city:
1. The car wash is currently on the FAR LEFT ABOVE the horizontal west road, immediately beside the parking lot. MOVE that whole recognizable blue-roof wash arch with pink brushes and yellow car to the FAR LEFT BELOW that horizontal road, between the road and the construction yard. The parking lot and barrier must remain above the road. Put the car wash at the same horizontal level as the top half of the center park's lower road segment. Keep the construction yard further down, close to the tram line. Do not block the road or tram. Let the old car wash location become a modest planted pavement pocket beside the parking lot, no extra building.
2. Inside the park, the Ferris wheel should be in the BACK-RIGHT quadrant (above the fountain's horizontal center), and the small wind turbine should be in the FRONT-RIGHT quadrant (below and slightly to the right of the wheel), opposite their current north-south order. The fountain and kitten path stay in place, keep open space around these three attractions.
Do not add labels, text, UI, additional bridges, duplicate car washes or duplicate wheels. This is still one coherent premium children's 3D toy-town concept, not a technical diagram.
